quest.title: Where Is the Unseen Razor?
quest.description: Lan has been looking for a certain sword. Her search has not been fruitful, so she's decided to widen her search range.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: ...You really don't have anything to do, do you? Either you're too good at what you do, or hopelessly inadequate...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: I doubt it's the latter though — you've been doing a fine job with my Commissions so far.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: If you're at a loose end, there is something else you could do for me.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: But this time things are more dangerous. I need you to defeat a Ruin Hunter. Think you can handle it?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: My, you are self-assured. My brother was the same way... Perhaps you will one day achieve the heights of greatness that he did.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: That's all. The location is Guili Plains. Get yourself ready, then go and take down that Ruin Hunter.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Once you've taken him down, remember to look around for sword-related items; anything you find, bring it back.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: ...But if there's nothing, just bring yourself.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Good luck with the Commission, and... I hope this time the search will prove more fruitful.

choices.text: Should I keep an eye out for a sword?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Yes please. When you've defeated the Ruin Hunter, please check around for a sword or any sword-related items.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I must warn you that Ruin Hunters are tough opponents. You must keep your attention fixed on them at all times if you wish to defeat them.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: And as for the sword — it would be wonderful if you found something, but not to worry if you don't. You will be paid as long as you defeat the Ruin Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Has the Ruin Hunter been dealt with?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Well, take your time. One must be fully prepared before taking on a Ruin Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Has the Ruin Hunter been dealt with?

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ruin Hunters are all in a day's work for you, eh... If I ever had any doubt in your capabilities, it is now gone.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: ...Still nothing on the sword? *sigh* I'm beginning to loathe the sound of my voice asking that question.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Not to worry. I've thrown a mixed bag of Commissions at you, and each time you complete them dutifully. So thank you for that.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Unseen Razor, where are you hiding...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: ...Are you trying to make me feel better? Thanks, but this is barely a minor setback.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: No matter how long it takes, and where this search takes me... I will find that sword.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I plan to keep widening the search area, so I may well call for your help again in future — and yes, I will continue to pay you for your services.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Here is your payment. I should go, there is a new list of Commissions waiting for me to vet.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Unseen Razor... You won't stay unseen forever...

choices.text: These Commissions don't seem sword-related at all.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: That is because I already took on every single Commission that had anything at all to do with a sword. Sadly, they led me nowhere.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: So then I thought... Surely, whatever happened to separate my brother from his sword, it can only have been under highly dangerous circumstances.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: So I started accepting other Commissions — ones I thought just might be dangerous enough to give me a lead on the whereabouts of Unseen Razor.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: However, there are slightly too many dangerous Commissions for me to handle on my own. That is why I started asking you to help.
